To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Pareto optimal learning schedule in cumulative evolution is unlikely to emerge as a result of individual fitness maximization if there is trade off between learning and exploiting, and that collapse of a fully developed cultural level is predicted by a selfish behavior of individuals in the game theoretical analysis.

(1) a learning schedule by which individuals learn more at earlier stages and less at later stages of their life is unlikely to evolve if there exists a negative correlation between learning and exploitation; and (2) the evolutionarily stable learning and exploitation schedules in a constant environment are different from those that are Pareto optimal in a sense that the former is less exploitive and more learning oriented than the latter.
the learning schedule that maximizes fitness in a constant environment is different from the one that is optimal for the realization of cumulative cultural evolution.

cultural evolution is not necessarily the same as biological evolution, and that the former is not always the same as the latter.
the learning and exploitation schedule that is optimal for the evolution of culture is different from the one that is optimal for maximizing the fitness of individuals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of learning schedule is not a trivial problem.
cumulative cultural evolution is not a natural consequence of individual learning and social transmission.
cultural evolution is a complex phenomenon that is not easily explained by the maximization principle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal learning schedule that maximizes the cultural level is not the evolutionarily stable strategy in the case of a trade off between learning and exploiting.
a trade-off between learning and exploiting may lead to the collapse of a fully developed cultural knowledge.
a trade-off between learning and exploitation is a necessary condition for the emergence of cumulative cultural evolution in our model.
